body.statement:
For replacement-adjacent samples, the explicitly calibrated \(\mathsf M_{h,k,J_\pi,J_\mu}^{\mathrm{DP}}\) and \(C_n(h,k)\) are \((\epsilon_n,\delta_n)\)-differentially private.  The accountant is adaptive parallel composition across \(D_\pi,D_\mu,D_*\), one joint Gaussian mechanism within each block, and post-processing thereafter.  There is a constant \(C_\Delta\), depending only on \((d,\kappa,\alpha,\beta,\gamma)\) and the fixed basis normalizations, such that, conditional on the projected pilots, the main joint moment statistic has replacement \(\ell_2\)-sensitivity at most
\[
 {C_\Delta\over m}\{h^{-d}+k h^{-2d}\},
\]
uniformly over \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{att}}\).
body.justification: Every pilot and every higher-order moment is protected under one explicit replacement-privacy accountant.
body.gap: SchroederMelnychukFeuerriegel2025 privatizes ordinary orthogonal CATE learners; it does not bound the sensitivity of a localized quadratic correction with shrinking bandwidth and growing basis dimension.
body.consumer: Privacy officers can audit the release ledger without treating nuisance fits or the quadratic correction as unprotected preprocessing.
body.proof_tex:
Fix \(n\ge 12\), \(h\in(0,r_0]\), \(k\ge1\), and the two positive integer pilot dimensions.  Then \(m=\lfloor n/3\rfloor\ge4\), so the ordered quadratic average in \(\mathrm{def{:}private\text{-}higher\text{-}order\text{-}learner}\) is well defined.  The privacy domain specified there is
\[
 \mathcal O_0=[0,1]^d\times\{0,1\}\times[0,1].
\]
This is also the almost-sure support of an observed record under every \(Q\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{att}}\): by \(\mathrm{ass{:}consistency}\),
\[
 Y=A Y(1)+(1-A)Y(0),
\]
and \(\mathrm{ass{:}bounded\text{-}outcomes}\) makes the right-hand side an element of \([0,1]\) almost surely.  The differential-privacy argument below in fact holds on all of \(\mathcal O_0^n\), independently of the data-generating law.

First fix realizations of the two projected pilots \((\bar\pi,\bar\mu)\).  If the projection sets in \(\mathrm{def{:}private\text{-}higher\text{-}order\text{-}learner}\) are nonempty, membership of the projections in those sets gives the pointwise bounds below.  If a set is empty, the prescribed fallback gives the same bounds because \(0<\kappa<1/2\).  Thus in every case
\[
 \kappa\le \bar\pi(x)\le1-\kappa,
 \qquad 0\le\bar\mu(x)\le1
 \quad (x\in\mathcal X).
\]
Consequently, for \(o=(x,a,y)\in\mathcal O_0\), every scalar factor among
\[
 a,\quad a-\bar\pi(x),\quad a\{a-\bar\pi(x)\},
 \quad y-\bar\mu(x)
\]
has absolute value at most one.  The same assertion holds for the primed record.  Write \(c_\rho\) and \(c_b\) for the deterministic basis constants in the construction.  Since \(K_h(x)\le h^{-d}\), and since Euclidean vectorization preserves the Frobenius norm, the two components of the linear kernel satisfy
\[
 \|\operatorname{vec}L_Q(o)\|_2\le c_\rho^2h^{-d},
 \qquad
 \|L_R(o)\|_2\le c_\rho h^{-d}.
\]
It follows, with \(c_L=(c_\rho^4+c_\rho^2)^{1/2}\), that
\[
 \|L(o)\|_2\le c_Lh^{-d}.
\]
For the quadratic kernel, Cauchy--Schwarz and the stated normalization of \(b_{h,k}\) give, whenever both basis factors can be nonzero,
\[
 \left|b_{h,k}(x)^{\mathsf T}b_{h,k}(x')\right|
 \le \|b_{h,k}(x)\|_2\|b_{h,k}(x')\|_2
 \le c_b^2 k h^{-d}.
\]
If either factor is off \(C_h\), the inner product is zero by the support condition on \(b_{h,k}\), so this bound remains valid globally.  Hence
\[
 \|\operatorname{vec}H_Q(o,o')\|_2
 \le c_b^2c_\rho^2 k h^{-2d},
 \qquad
 \|H_R(o,o')\|_2
 \le c_b^2c_\rho k h^{-2d}.
\]
Thus, for \(c_H=c_b^2(c_\rho^4+c_\rho^2)^{1/2}\), the deterministic clipping radii in the construction obey
\[
 \Lambda_L\le c_Lh^{-d},
 \qquad
 \Lambda_H\le c_Hkh^{-2d}.
\]
These inequalities are uniform over every admissible value of the projected pilots and hence over \(Q\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{att}}\).

Consider two replacement-adjacent main-block samples \(D_*\) and \(D_*'\), differing only at index \(r\).  Every clipped linear summand has norm at most \(\Lambda_L\), so the difference of the two linear averages has norm at most \(2\Lambda_L/m\).  In the ordered quadratic sum, precisely the \(2(m-1)\) ordered pairs \((r,j)\) and \((j,r)\), \(j\ne r\), can change.  Every clipped quadratic summand has norm at most \(\Lambda_H\), and therefore the difference between its old and new values has norm at most \(2\Lambda_H\).  The triangle inequality now yields
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \|T_*(D_*)-T_*(D_*')\|_2
 &\le {2\Lambda_L\over m}
   +{2(m-1)\,2\Lambda_H\over m(m-1)}\\
 &= {2\Lambda_L+4\Lambda_H\over m}\\
 &\le {C_\Delta\over m}\{h^{-d}+kh^{-2d}\},
\end{aligned}
\]
where
\[
 C_\Delta=\max\{2c_L,4c_H\}.
\]
This is a deterministic conditional sensitivity bound.  Its constant depends only on \((d,\kappa,\alpha,\beta,\gamma)\) and the fixed basis normalizations (indeed the displayed choice only uses their constants), as required.

We next verify every Gaussian calibration.  For \(u\in\{\pi,\mu\}\), replacement of one record in its pilot block changes the unnoised average by
\[
 \left\|{1\over m}\sum_{i=1}^m z_u(O_i)
      -{1\over m}\sum_{i=1}^m z_u(O_i')\right\|_2
 ={1\over m}\|z_u(o)-z_u(o')\|_2
 \le\Delta_u
\]
by the definition of \(\Delta_u\).  The supremum is finite because the fixed finite-dimensional tensor-spline coordinates are bounded on the compact cube and \((a,y)\in\{0,1\}\times[0,1]\).  The preceding main-block calculation shows in the same way that \(\overline\Delta_*=(2\Lambda_L+4\Lambda_H)/m\) is a valid replacement sensitivity bound conditional on the pilots.

The symbol assumptions give \(0<\epsilon_n\le1\) and \(0<\delta_n<1/2\).  Therefore
\[
 0<\epsilon_n^\circ=\min\{\epsilon_n,1/2\}<1,
 \qquad
 c_{\delta_n}=\sqrt{2\log(1.25/\delta_n)}+1
 >\sqrt{2\log(1.25/\delta_n)}.
\]
Applying \(\mathrm{lem{:}gaussian\text{-}mechanism\text{-}replacement}\) to each pilot average proves that each pilot release is \((\epsilon_n^\circ,\delta_n)\)-differentially private on its own block.  Conditional on any fixed pilot realization, applying the same lemma to \(T_*\) and \(\overline\Delta_*\) proves that the main release is \((\epsilon_n^\circ,\delta_n)\)-differentially private on \(D_*\).

It remains to show that the adaptive use of the pilots does not add the three budgets.  Denote the two pilot releases by \(Z_\pi^{\mathrm{rel}},Z_\mu^{\mathrm{rel}}\) and the main release by \(W^{\mathrm{rel}}\), and consider the full internal transcript
\[
 \mathcal T=(Z_\pi^{\mathrm{rel}},Z_\mu^{\mathrm{rel}},W^{\mathrm{rel}}).
\]
If adjacent full samples differ in \(D_*\), the joint law \(\nu\) of the pilot releases is unchanged.  For any measurable transcript event \(E\), let \(E_z\) be its section at pilot value \(z\), and let \(K_D(z,\cdot)\) be the conditional law of the main release.  Conditional main-block privacy gives
\[
 K_D(z,E_z)\le e^{\epsilon_n^\circ}K_{D'}(z,E_z)+\delta_n
 \quad\text{for every }z.
\]
Integration against the common law \(\nu\) gives
\[
 \Pr_D(\mathcal T\in E)
 \le e^{\epsilon_n^\circ}\Pr_{D'}(\mathcal T\in E)+\delta_n.
\]

If the changed record lies in \(D_\pi\), condition on the unchanged blocks \((D_\mu,D_*)\).  Once \(Z_\pi^{\mathrm{rel}}=z\) is fixed, drawing \(Z_\mu^{\mathrm{rel}}\), constructing both projected pilots, and drawing the main release defines a Markov kernel \(K(z,\cdot)\) that is identical for the two adjacent values of \(D_\pi\).  For a measurable transcript event \(E\), put \(g(z)=K(z,E)\in[0,1]\).  The event form of pilot privacy also controls bounded measurable functions: by the layer-cake identity and the privacy inequality for each set \(\{g>t\}\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \int g\,d\mathsf P_D
 &=\int_0^1\mathsf P_D\{g>t\}\,dt\\
 &\le\int_0^1
   \left(e^{\epsilon_n^\circ}\mathsf P_{D'}\{g>t\}+\delta_n\right)dt\\
 &=e^{\epsilon_n^\circ}\int g\,d\mathsf P_{D'}+\delta_n.
\end{aligned}
\]
This is exactly the privacy inequality for the full transcript.  The argument for a replacement in \(D_\mu\) is identical.  If the replaced record is among the at most two discarded observations, the transcript is unchanged.  These four exhaustive cases prove adaptive parallel composition:
\[
 \mathcal T\text{ is replacement }(\epsilon_n^\circ,\delta_n)\text{-differentially private}.
\]
Because \(\epsilon_n^\circ\le\epsilon_n\), monotonicity of the defining inequality in its first parameter makes \(\mathcal T\) replacement \((\epsilon_n,\delta_n)\)-differentially private.

Finally, reconstruction of the pilot functions, metric projection, spectral flooring, matrix inversion, and evaluation at \(x_0\) are measurable functions of the transcript and public tuning parameters.  For any such measurable map \(F\) and event \(B\), applying the transcript privacy inequality to \(F^{-1}(B)\) proves the same privacy inequality for \(F(\mathcal T)\).  Thus the returned \(\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{DP}}(x_0;h,k)\), and hence \(\mathsf M_{h,k,J_\pi,J_\mu}^{\mathrm{DP}}\), are \((\epsilon_n,\delta_n)\)-differentially private.  The radius in \(\mathrm{def{:}private\text{-}confidence\text{-}interval}\) is deterministic given the public parameters, and interval formation and intersection with \([-1,1]\) are further measurable post-processing.  Therefore \(C_n(h,k)\) has the same replacement privacy guarantee.
